project.name: blogagent-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for the blog generation agent (V9 §18 / §91).
Members. BlogAgentPort (5 methods), plus the three narrowed records it carries: BlogAgentTaskDraft (write), BlogAgentTaskView (read), BlogAgentPostView (read).
Why the module exists. Four statements in three files reached into blogagent's application layer, and two more reached into its api layer:
agent -> blogagent (4 impl / 2 api) BlogGenerationTool, PublishPostTool, ImageGenerationTool agent -> publishing (0 impl / 1 api) PublishPostTool
BlogGenerationTool and PublishPostTool imported blogagent.application.BlogAgentService together with blogagent.api.*, and PublishPostTool additionally imported publishing.api.BlogPostVO, because that is what BlogAgentService.publish returns. After the split dinqor-agent could not be built without blogagent's implementation classes AND without publishing's api layer.
What this cut takes. The SERVICE capability -- the two tools that go through BlogAgentService. It clears agent -> publishing outright (PublishPostTool was the only cross-domain reader of BlogPostVO) and shortens agent -> blogagent from 4 to 2.
What it deliberately does NOT take. ImageGenerationTool's two statements, which reach into blogagent.infrastructure (BlogAgentImageClient, BlogAgentProperties). That is a different shape from a service port -- a concrete client plus a @ConfigurationProperties bean -- and it carries its own decision: the generated image travels as bytes and the token usage travels as a three-long record, because ModelUsage lives in libs/xander-model and a contract may not depend on a library that drags in Jackson (ADR-1). Settling that shape is a separate cut, so agent -> blogagent does not reach zero here.
Why the DTOs are NARROWED, not mirrored. The mirror rule (ADR §2.5) exists for a type that *replaces* a frontend-visible one: mirroring then makes "serialization is byte-identical" provable, which is what keeps the cut a pure refactor. Nothing here replaces anything. blogagent.api.BlogAgentTaskVO stays exactly where it is and keeps going to the frontend unchanged from blogagent.api.BlogAgentController; so does publishing.api.BlogPostVO. Every type in this module is new, on a new seam the frontend never sees, so each carries exactly the components its consumers read:
BlogAgentTaskView 4 of the domain entity's 25 id, title, summary, publishedPostId BlogAgentPostView 5 of BlogPostVO's 17 id, title, status, csdnSynced, juejinSynced BlogAgentTaskDraft mirrors BlogAgentTaskCreateRequest's 2 fields, without @NotBlank
What IS pinned is the component order, by reflection, and the mapping entity/VO -> record, by an app-module test using mutually distinct literals.
Why jakarta.validation annotations are NOT here. blogagent.api.BlogAgentTaskCreateRequest carries @NotBlank and @Size, and those fire only because BlogAgentController annotates the parameter @Valid. A contract may not carry them anyway (they would add a dependency, and ADR-1 keeps this module framework-free). Nothing is lost on the agent path, which never had them: the tools build their arguments from JSON, and BlogAgentService validates the fields itself in normalizeClientRequestId. BlogAgentTaskDraft mirrors the request's two fields without the annotations, and the domain-side request type stays the validated front door for the HTTP callers.
Why every method takes the caller id FIRST. All four earlier contracts do, and the guard test that pins it asserts the first parameter's TYPE is Long -- which is a weaker statement than the invariant it is named for. Four of the five methods this port wraps declare their parameters the other way round on the provider side (publish(taskId, userId), findPublishedPost(taskId, userId), runStream(taskId, userId, ...)), so mirroring the provider's order would have made the port inconsistent while still passing that guard. Instead the port normalises to (userId, ...) and the provider's thin adapters swap explicitly, one line each, pinned by a mapping test whose two literals differ (42 vs 9). BlogAgentPortTest asserts the first parameter is NAMED userId, not merely typed Long -- javac is run with -parameters here, so the name survives into the class file, and that closes the gap between what the guard says and what it checks.
Package note: this module's package is com.xander.lab.blogagent.spi, NOT com.xander.lab.blogagent.api. blogagent already owns com.xander.lab.blogagent.api as its *frontend HTTP* layer (BlogAgentController, BlogAgentTaskCreateRequest, BlogAgentTaskVO, BlogAgentSessionVO, BlogAgentMessageRequest). Declaring the contract there would put one package in two jars, and would make the scanner classify those controllers as shared kernel, turning "a controller imports its own application layer" into dozens of blogagent.api -> blogagent backlog edges plus a shared-kernel-reverse-dependency violation each. Same collision as agent-api, automation-api, recitation-api and studio-api; same answer. SHARED_KERNEL lists blogagent.spi (dotted, matched longest-first, so it does not swallow blogagent.application, blogagent.domain or blogagent.infrastructure).
What is deliberately NOT here yet: - ImageGenerationTool's image capability (see above). - generateTopicSeries, whose only caller is automation.BlogContentPlanService -- same deployment unit (both are dinqor-content-automation), so converting it would move no cross-unit metric. It is a candidate for a later tidy-up, not for this cut. - listSessions / reviseStream / reviewCompliance / findTaskByClientRequestId: their callers are BlogAgentController and BlogAgentService's own pipeline. - Any of blogagent's own api layer (com.xander.lab.blogagent.api.*). It is the frontend HTTP contract, a different audience, and it joins a contract module only when that layer itself is split in Wave 2.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine.
